node.title: Re: regex to match "---" followed by new line
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Your regex does seem to do something for me... but what does your $text contain? If you're reading it from a file, are you reading the file line-by-line or are you slurping it all at once? There are several things I could point out about the regex, like how I'm not sure what (.{0,0})\K is supposed to be doing, or that the dots . will match anything, including newlines (because of /s) and dashes. But reviewing the regex doesn't make much sense without knowing what it's supposed to match against - please provide an [id://1177642|SSCCE] with several examples of what should match and what shouldn't!

use Data::Dump; dd "--- Foo --- Bar " =~ /(.{0,0})\K(---\s*)(.{0,200})/gisx; __END__ ("", "--- ", "Foo --- Bar ")

Also, note that you could set the input record separator [doc://$/] to something like "--- " to read a file in chunks separated by that string.
